dm.story_so_far: The Lantern Wall searched dead choirmaster Mr Abel's lodging beneath their own loft. Ada's critical Read showed that the cramped lower hand on the hymn sheet is the choir writing through Abel, a verse ahead, signed Maren, who drowned with the chapel. It is the same voice that sang her mother's name for her. Cass picked the salt-crusted cabinet cleanly: inside were dry choir surplices, a ring of seven green-iron bell-tower keys (Cass has them) and a set of handbells, one slot empty and wet. Dev read the daybook as the tower's change book, one change short and waiting for a ringer, with his grandmother Maren's name in the margin. The book wants him to supply the last row. From the window Bram saw choir-white figures on the chandler's slates, all of them turning to face the tide. A salt hand cracked the glass under his hand and left him a Bleed mark. Then the harmonium stopped and the tide turned. A black bell tower now stands out on the flats where the rope was, the water is coming in fast, and the choir is on its second-to-last verse. The circle is racing through the mud to the tower.
